key_insight: Use structured world models as training-free priors to guide which preference dimensions to query, enabling efficient multi-turn cold-start personalization without per-user training.
problem_solved: How to infer a new user's few relevant preferences from many possible dimensions under a tight question budget — the routing problem of selecting which questions actually matter for each user.
method: Construct structured world models that encode relationships between tasks, contexts, and preference dimensions as priors (no per-user training required).
Use planning/decision procedures over the world model to route limited queries toward dimensions most likely to influence the user’s outcomes.
Drive a lightweight interaction policy that selects questions and actions based on the model’s priors, adapting in multi-turn conversations to quickly identify salient preferences.
impact: Provides a practical, training-free approach to cold-start personalization, reducing required user interaction and accelerating deployment of personalized systems where historical user data is unavailable.
visual_elements: Routing diagram: many preference dimensions (nodes) with the model highlighting the few queried dimensions for a given user.
Flowchart: structured world model -> planner -> question selection -> user response loop (multi-turn cycle).
Bar/line chart: number of questions vs. preference recovery accuracy comparing training-free priors to random or generic baselines.
Icons: user avatar + question bubbles + model/brain icon to signal zero-shot priors and reduced interaction cost.
paper_title: Cold-Start Personalization via Training-Free Priors from Structured World Models
paper_authors: Avinandan Bose, Shuyue Stella Li, Faeze Brahman, Pang Wei Koh, Simon Shaolei Du
